_comment: Single source of truth for the press page. Edit this file, then run
python3 scripts/update-press.py
to render the cards into press.html.
5. Each 'shot' is a screenshot of the article itself, captured at phone
width with cookie banners dismissed and ad slots hidden, then stored
under public/images/press-shots/. Recapture with scripts/capture-press.md.
RULES FOR THIS FILE, which matter more than usual because the content is
other people's writing:
1. Every 'quote' is VERBATIM from the article at 'url'. Not a paraphrase,
not a tidied version, not a sentence assembled from two places. Each one
below was checked by loading the live article and asserting the string
appears in the page text character for character (allowing only for
curly quotes and dashes).
2. A quote is a COMPLETE sentence. A fragment cut to fit is a misquote.
3. No quote, no problem: omit the field and the card renders as a citation
with a link. Never invent one to fill the gap.
4. Every 'url' has been fetched and confirmed to load and to be about this
property. Several URLs on the old version of this page did not: two
redirected to unrelated articles (a football report and a boxing
preview) because their article IDs were invented, and nine returned 404.
Do not add a URL that has not been opened.
'checked' is when the whole set was last verified end to end.
'screen' is the television and film coverage, shown as click-to-load video
cards. The thumbnail is stored under public/images/press-video/ rather than
hotlinked from i.ytimg.com, and the YouTube player is only inserted once a
visitor presses play -- cookies.html says third-party cookies apply once you
arrive at their site, and an iframe on load would quietly make that untrue.
Shot URLs carry a ?v= stamp because Railway sends no cache-control header:
a recaptured clipping keeps its filename, so without the stamp a returning
visitor would keep the old one. Bump it when you recapture.
Every entry carries a 'date' and a 'dateKind'. For articles that is the
publication date from the page's own metadata. For videos it is the YouTube
upload date, which is NOT the broadcast date: two of the programmes aired
years before the channel posted the clip in August 2026. The cards label
them differently for that reason, and the combined feed sorts on this field.
